expectations.evidence: Section 3.1 explicitly names all four levels: VS-NfD, VS-VERTRAULICH, GEHEIM, and STRENG GEHEIM, noting the platform does NOT process the higher three levels.

Section 2.1 provides extensive IT-Grundschutz detail: BSI-Standards 200-1 through 200-4, the Kompendium structure (ISMS, ORP, CON, OPS, DER, INF, NET, SYS, APP), a table of 20+ specific Bausteine with relevance descriptions, and Appendix B lists detailed Bausteine per layer.

Section 2.1 explains C5:2020 with all 17 criteria domains listed, Typ 1 vs Typ 2 attestation types defined, and Section 15.5 details the C5 audit process: engaging a Wirtschaftspruefungsgesellschaft, ISAE 3402-based examination, 6-12 month observation period for Typ 2, and the attestation report.

Section 10 provides a full analysis: Section 10.1 lists mandatory BSI-approved products (VPN, crypto, remote access), Section 10.2 lists strongly recommended (firewall, HSM, IDS, MFA tokens), Section 10.3 lists where FLOSS is fully acceptable (20+ components), and Section 10.4 provides a decision tree.

Section 8.2 is dedicated to the Kryptokonzept per CON.1, references BSI TR-02102-1 as primary reference, lists approved algorithms with key lengths (AES, SHA-256/384/512/SHA3, ECDHE with Brainpool curves, RSA>=3000 bit), and Appendix A lists TR-02102-1 through TR-02102-4 and TR-03116.

Section 3.2 defines six absolute requirements: all data at rest within Germany, BSI-approved encryption for transit within German infrastructure, no foreign cloud, no hyperscaler, German-located personnel. Section 3.3 includes a diagram with 'NO DATA CROSSES THIS BOUNDARY'. GDPR/DSGVO and BDSG listed in Section 2.2.

Section 2.1 lists Bausteine organized by layer (ISMS, ORP, CON, OPS, DER, INF, NET, SYS, APP) with a table of specific modules. Section 15 details the full methodology: Strukturanalyse, Schutzbedarfsfeststellung (normal/hoch/sehr hoch), Modellierung, IT-Grundschutz-Check with status categories (ja/teilweise/nein/entbehrlich), and BSI-Standard 200-3 risk analysis. Certification as ISO 27001 auf Basis von IT-Grundschutz.

Section 10 provides nuanced three-tier analysis: mandatory BSI-approved (VPN, crypto for VS-NfD transit), strongly recommended (perimeter firewall, HSM, IDS), and fully FLOSS-appropriate (20+ components with required Grundschutz Bausteine mapped). Includes a decision tree and ADR-003 explains the rationale for the VPN boundary.

Section 9 maps OpenStack services to the architecture. Section 10.3 maps OpenStack to SYS.1.5 and APP-specific Bausteine. Section 15.3 maps specific OpenStack components to applicable Bausteine (control plane to APP/SYS.1.1/SYS.1.3, KVM hypervisors to SYS.1.5). Section 5.2 details hypervisor hardening per BSI SYS.1.5.

Section 2.2 lists NIS2 Directive, GDPR/DSGVO, eIDAS. Section 2.3 covers NIS2 transposition via NIS2UmsuCG, EUCS as emerging certification scheme, and GDPR. Section 19.1 provides a table with GDPR, NIS2, EUCS, and eIDAS status and impact.

Section 15 presents a six-phase lifecycle: Kategorisierung (Strukturanalyse), Select (Modellierung), Implement (Umsetzung), Assess (Audit), Certify/Attest, and Continuous Monitoring. Details 3-year certificate validity, annual surveillance audits, re-certification, and significant-change re-assessment triggers.

Executive summary explicitly states BSI IT-Grundschutz as primary baseline, 'not DISA STIGs or CIS Benchmarks as the primary reference.' Section 11.2 lists CIS and DISA STIGs as supplementary/informational only. All frameworks, terminology, and processes use German BSI standards as authoritative. No FedRAMP, NIST 800-53, or US frameworks appear as primary references.
